record.context_brief: Gap structure in attainable j-primitive degrees
record.original_question: Fix integers m >= 2, n >= 2, and j in [n]. Let A be a nonnegative tensor of order m and dimension n, and let M(A) denote its majorization matrix, defined by M(A)_{ij} = a_{ij...j}. Call A j-primitive if there exists a positive integer k such that (M(A^k))_{u j} > 0 for every u in [n], and let γ_j(A) be the least such k. Define R_j(m, n) to be the set of integers k for which there exists a nonnegative tensor A of order m and dimension n that is j-primitive but not primitive, with γ_j(A) = k. Does the set R_j(m, n) have gaps, meaning missing integers between two values that do occur?

evidence.quote: The majorization matrix M(A) of the tensor A is defined as (M(A))ij = aij...j, i, j in [n].

For a fixed integer j in [n], if there exists a positive integer k such that (M(A^k))_{u j} > 0, for all u in [n], then A is called j-primitive and the smallest such integer k is called the j-primitive degree of A, denoted by γ_j(A).
R_j(m, n) = {k | there exists a nonnegative but not primitive tensor A of order m dimension n such that A is j-primitive and γ_j(A) = k}.
Question 4.12. Does there exist gaps in R_j(m, n)?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Fix integers $m\ge 2$ and $n\ge 2$, and let $[n]=\{1,2,\dots,n\}$. A tensor $A=(a_{i_1 i_2\cdots i_m})$ of order $m$ and dimension $n$ is a real array indexed by $(i_1,\dots,i_m)\in[n]^m$, and is called nonnegative if all its entries are nonnegative. The product $A^k$ (in the sense used for nonnegative tensor primitivity) is defined recursively so that for any tensor $B$ of order $m$ and dimension $n$, the entries of $AB$ are $(AB)_{i j_2\cdots j_m}=\sum_{i_2,\dots,i_m\in[n]} a_{i i_2\cdots i_m}\, b_{i_2 j_2\cdots j_m}\cdots$ (the standard tensor power yielding again a tensor of the same format).

The majorization matrix $M(A)$ of $A$ is the $n\times n$ matrix with entries $M(A)_{ij}=a_{i j j\cdots j}$ for $i,j\in[n]$.

The tensor $A$ is called primitive if there exists a positive integer $k$ such that all entries of $M(A^k)$ are positive. For a fixed $j\in[n]$, $A$ is called $j$-primitive if there exists a positive integer $k$ such that $(M(A^k))_{u j}>0$ for every $u\in[n]$; the least such $k$ is the $j$-primitive degree $\gamma_j(A)$.

Define
$$R_j(m,n)=\{k\in\mathbb{Z}_{>0}: \text{ there exists a nonnegative tensor }A\text{ of order }m\text{ and dimension }n\text{ that is }j\text{-primitive but not primitive, with }\gamma_j(A)=k\}.$$

Question: Does $R_j(m,n)$ have gaps? That is, do there exist integers $a<b<c$ with $a,c\in R_j(m,n)$ but $b\notin R_j(m,n)$?
artifact.status_search_result: A web search did not surface a paper resolving the gap structure of the set $R_j(m,n)$ of attainable $j$-primitive degrees of nonnegative but non-primitive tensors. Related works on primitive degrees of nonnegative tensors and directed hypergraphs exist, but no conclusive result on the existence or non-existence of gaps in $R_j(m,n)$ was found.
